POST /api/imports/customers creates every imported user with the hardcoded password "changeme123". Anyone who knows this value (it is in source and never forced to change) can log in as any imported customer account; dispatchers (allowed to call this endpoint, although direct user creation at POST /api/users/ is ops_admin-only) can also take over the accounts they import.

POST /api/imports/jobs accepts dispatchers but, unlike create_job (jobs.py:102-108), performs no DispatcherRegion permission check on the imported row's region_id, allowing a dispatcher to create jobs in regions they are not assigned to.

GET /api/audit-logs/job/{job_id} requires only that the caller be a dispatcher or field worker — there is no check that the job belongs to the worker, or is in the dispatcher's region (unlike every other job-scoped endpoint). Any worker/dispatcher can read audit trails (including IP addresses, user identities and action details, via AuditLogOut) for arbitrary jobs.

GET /api/routes/{route_id} enforces ownership for field workers and region scoping for dispatchers, but has no branch for customers — any customer can read any route. RouteOut embeds stops[].job as full JobOut (schemas.py:253), leaking other customers' job internal_notes, descriptions and service location details.
